# artifactkeeper_repository_routing_rules (Resource)

Ordered path-rewrite rules applied to a repository's proxy requests. A singleton keyed by repository key: a write replaces the whole ordered list, and destroying it clears every rule. Rules are evaluated in order, first match wins, so list order is significant.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Ordered path-rewrite rules for a remote repository's proxy requests. Rules are
# evaluated top to bottom, first match wins, so list order matters.
resource "artifactkeeper_repository_routing_rules" "npm_proxy" {
  repository_key = artifactkeeper_repository.npm_proxy.key
  rules = [
    {
      path_pattern = "^/v1/(.*)$"
      rewrite_to   = "/$1"
    },
    {
      path_pattern = "^/legacy/(.*)$"
      rewrite_to   = "/new/$1"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repository_key` (String) Key of the repository whose routing rules are managed. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `rules` (Attributes List) Ordered list of rewrite rules. Evaluated top to bottom, first match wins. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier. Equal to `repository_key`, since the rules are a singleton per repository.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `path_pattern` (String) Pattern matched against the incoming request path.
- `rewrite_to` (String) Path the request is rewritten to when the pattern matches.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import artifactkeeper_repository_routing_rules.npm_proxy npm-remote
```
